subject: Sustained 5xx spike & throughput degradation — remediation + commercial proposal
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@heliohealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, support@redwood.com
Cc: Helio Health Oncall <oncall@heliohealth.com>
Date: Thu, 9 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: nightly batch 5xx spike + throughput drop (impacting /infer)

Hi Jonas / Redwood team,

We experienced a sustained spike in 5xx errors starting ~08:50 PST on 2028-05-09 that hit our nightly batch inference jobs. Throughput dropped ~42% and tail latency doubled; several of our clinical pipelines timed out and queued. We attached the Helio side logs (helio_service_report_q2_logs.csv) and included our on-call.

This is high-severity for us — these jobs are time-sensitive for clinical reporting. Please provide:
- immediate mitigation (short term)
- root cause & ETA to full restoration
- commercial remediation (SLA credits or refund) and how you will prevent recurrence

We need exec-level visibility and a proposed remediation/credit within 8 business hours.

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Data Platform
Helio Health

Attachments: helio_service_report_q2_logs.csv (csv)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 May 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production: nightly batch 5xx spike + throughput drop (impacting /infer)

Team — forwarding Helio escalation. Quick summary of the telemetry I saw: sustained 5xxs tied to our autoscaler not provisioning warm pods for their large-batch window; combined with a KV-cache thrash during multipass requests, causing GC/backpressure on the serving nodes and token generation timeouts. Impact window observed 08:50–09:35 PST, with periodic recurrence through 09:50.

Immediate asks:
- Ben: need commercial posture and approval for an above-threshold make-good (they want credits). Suggest we offer a one-time commercial remediation and short free burst capacity.
- Evelyn: please own customer comms (ack + timeline) and coordinate CS remediation steps.
- Laura: can you confirm capacity options (burst pool / reserved capacity switch) and whether we can grant a free 2x burst for their May billing cycle? Attach: impact_timeline_may09.csv

I will draft the customer-facing remediation + credit proposal once we agree posture.

Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Attachments: impact_timeline_may09.csv (csv)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 May 2028 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: nightly batch 5xx spike + throughput drop (impacting /infer)

Thanks for the quick triage, Jonas. I support a remediation offer; commercial thinking below:
- One-time invoice credit equal to 30% of Helio's May invoice, capped at $100,000.
- Waive May overage fees and provide 3 months of free burst capacity (up to 2x baseline) to cover seasonal spikes while they evaluate our Dedicated reservation options.
- Fix + timeline and a commitment to a postmortem within 72 hours.

Ben
VP Sales — Redwood Inference

P.S. Jonas — draft the offer email (apology + root cause + timeline + credits) and include the PO/DocuSign path for the contract amendment. I can escalate for approval if needed but try to keep within the cap first.
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 May 2028 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed remediation & commercial make-good — Helio Health (incident 20280509)

Alicia —

First, sincere apologies for the impact to your nightly pipelines this morning. We take incidents like this seriously and appreciate the quick reports and logs you provided. Below is a concise remediation plan and our commercial proposal while we complete the postmortem.

Summary / root cause (short):
- Cause: Autoscaler warmup misconfiguration + cache eviction storms during Helio's high-concurrency batch window. This combination caused a backlog and generated transient 5xxs from token generation timeouts.
- Immediate fix applied at 11:00 PST: increased warm replica target for Helio's burst window, disabled an aggressive cache eviction path, and applied a hotfix to the scheduler to throttle request admission during the warmup. Error rate has returned to baseline on our metrics; we will continue to monitor for 48 hours.

Planned follow-ups / timeline:
- 24–48h: deploy durable autoscaler fix and additional KV-cache guardrails (Engineering).
- 72h: full postmortem with logs and long-form RCA delivered to your team.

Commercial remediation (proposal):
- One-time service credit: 30% of Helio's May 2028 invoice, capped at $100,000, applied as a credit on the next invoice.
- Waive May overage charges related to the incident window.
- Provide 3 months of free burst capacity (up to 2x their current baseline) to reduce risk while we complete mitigations.
- Optional: if Helio prefers, we will draft a contract amendment to include a tailored burst reservation and an adjusted SLO that better aligns with their large-batch windows.

Next steps we propose:
1) Please confirm receipt and whether the commercial package above is acceptable in principle.
2) If accepted, we will prepare a DocuSign contract amendment and a HubSpot deal update (deal HL-4821).
3) Schedule an exec call tomorrow for 30 minutes to review the postmortem draft.

Attached: redwood_helio_makegood_proposal.pdf (proposal + credit calculation example)

Again, deeply sorry for the disruption — we want to make this right. Evelyn will follow up on scheduling and Laura will coordinate burst capacity.

—Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposed remediation & commercial make-good — Helio Health (incident 20280509)

Jonas, Ben, Evelyn — thank you for the rapid response and the clear plan. Helio accepts the commercial package in principle: the one-time 30% credit (cap $100k), waived May overages, and the 3-month free burst capacity. We do want the contract amendment to include a clause around guaranteed pre-warm capacity during our nightly window and a faster SLO for batch job 95th percentile latency. Please include a DocuSign link for our legal team and let's schedule the exec call tomorrow at 10:00 AM PST.

We expect the postmortem within 72 hours and will review the draft with our on-call.

Alicia Gomez
Head of Data Platform — Helio Health
